title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an 'algebra of figures'. L is a set of 'points'. A figure is an ordered set 𝓕 of subsets A ⊂ L (the 'stables' or closed strata). Each A carries a 'multiplicity' or sub-figure F_A, with interior A^0 = A \ ∂A. On the previous page he notes that 𝓕 can be replaced by sub-posets stable under ∩ (or under taking sub-figures) and under sup, cut out by conditions on the A's.

This page continues with two examples.

(1) Finiteness conditions. If one imposes a condition such as local finiteness, the resulting sub-poset F' is stable under finite sups but not, in general, under arbitrary sups. Definitions:
- A figure F is finite if it is finite as an ordered set, i.e. it has finitely many strata.
- It is of finite type if it is contained in a finite union of sub-figures F_A (the closures of strata).
- Claim: F is finite iff it is of finite type and its strata (closed strata F_A) are finite.

(2) Geometric realisation. Suppose L is a poset realised by a closed stratification (X_x)_{x∈L} of a topological space X by 'cells'. X is triangulable and has some adjective that is hard to read. In modern terms, L is the face poset of a regular CW (or cell) complex, with x ≤ y iff X_x ⊂ X_y. The margin note says the X_x form an 'admissible family' (a covering) of X. For A ⊂ L, put X_A = ⋃_{x∈A} X_x. Then A ↦ X_A is a bijection between:
- the admissible parts of L, namely the closed parts (down-sets for the Alexandrov topology), and
- the closed subsets of X saturated for the equivalence relation given by the partition of X into the open cells X_x^0.
'In fact all such parts' are obtained when L is finite.

Purpose: on the next page, figures whose strata are closed in L are reinterpreted as data on X ('subdivisions' of X). This prepares the definitions of refinement and subdivision between two set-theoretic figures, via the least element φ(A) of G^A.
errors: A ↦ X_A being a bijection onto all closed saturated subsets, and the closedness of X_A for an infinite down-set A, require local finiteness or a CW (weak) topology when L is infinite. Grothendieck signals this himself by restricting 'all parts of this type' to L finite. Not an error, but a stated gap.
The bijection also needs the cells to be regular, i.e. closure of X_x^0 = X_x = ⋃_{y≤x} X_y^0. This is implicit in 'stratification fermée par des cellules'.

ideas.what: Finite figures vs figures of finite type; finite iff finite type with finite closed strata; finite-sup stability but not arbitrary-sup stability of a sub-poset defined by finiteness
ideas.modern_name: finite / finite-type (locally finite) posets and stratifications, compact objects in the lattice of figures

ideas.what: Poset L realised as a closed cellular stratification of a triangulable space; closed (down-closed) subsets of L correspond bijectively to closed unions of cells (subcomplexes)
ideas.modern_name: face poset of a regular CW complex; Alexandrov topology; subcomplexes ↔ down-sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandroff (1937, Alexandrov topology); Björner (1984, regular CW complexes and face posets)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 'géométrie modérée' / stratified-spaces discussion in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not in this form

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine definitions (finite and finite-type figures) and the standard correspondence between down-sets of a face poset and subcomplexes of a regular cell complex. It is historically interesting as part of the unpublished 'algèbre des figures' (1986), but nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathcal{J}$' in line 3 is almost certainly '$\mathcal{F}$' (the poset of figures).
'à tout $A\in\mathcal{L}$' should read '$A\subset\mathcal{L}$' (A is a part of L).
'il[?] dans une stratification' is likely 'il[lustrée/réalisée] dans une stratification (fermée) X_x (x∈L) d'un espace topologique'.
'triangulable convexe[?]' is uncertain; it may be 'compact' or 'convenable'.
'On a trouvé[?] alors une partition[?] ... des fermés' probably reads 'On trouve alors que l'application, des parties [fermées] A de L, ... A ↦ X_A soit une bijection'.
The first line's 'muni d'une topologie' is doubtful from the image. The sense, given 'comme celle d'être localement fini', is a finiteness condition imposed on the A's.
